hearthstead.guide.title: Settler's Handbook
hearthstead.guide.page1.title: Founding
hearthstead.guide.page1.body: Craft a Settlement Hearth from logs, cobblestone and a campfire. Place it on open ground and keep the area safe. Within moments, three settlers will gather at the fire — your settlement is born, with its own name and a working radius around the hearth.
hearthstead.guide.page2.title: Settlers
hearthstead.guide.page2.body: Each settler has a name, hunger, energy and morale. Right-click a settler to see how they fare. They eat from the communal stores when hungry, rest by the fire at night, and flee to the hearth when danger comes.
hearthstead.guide.page3.title: Professions
hearthstead.guide.page3.body: Craft a writ from paper, string and a wooden tool. Use it on a settler to appoint them: Farmers harvest and replant nearby crops. Lumberers fell trees cleanly and replant saplings. Guards patrol and defend. Sneak-use a writ to relieve a settler. Writs are never consumed.
hearthstead.guide.page4.title: Needs & Morale
hearthstead.guide.page4.body: Keep bread and other food in the hearth — hungry settlers head there to eat. Settlers work through the day and rest at night. Well-fed, well-rested settlers grow joyful; neglect makes them miserable and slow to work.
hearthstead.guide.page5.title: Danger
hearthstead.guide.page5.body: When a monster strikes, the alarm bell rings. Civilians run for the hearth while guards draw steel and hunt the threat. Settlers can die — keep guards posted and the nights lit, and the settlement will mourn less often.
hearthstead.guide.page6.title: Growth
hearthstead.guide.page6.body: A well-supplied settlement spreads word. Keep at least 8 food in stores and morale content or better, and a traveler will appear at the edge of your lands, walking to the hearth to join you. Growth costs a little food — a small price for new hands.
